title: Accounts Assistant
description:
Accounts Assistant

Salary: £32,000

Location: Droitwich

Company Profile

This is an opportunity to join an established SME manufacturing business, providing hands-on finance support. The role will involve the day-to-day running of the accounts function, working closely with senior managers and assisting with a variety of transactional and month-end activities.

What's on Offer?
- Full-time, permanent position
- Office Based
- Varied role within a small, supportive business
- Exposure to a broad range of accounts and finance duties
- Opportunity to develop skills and progress within the finance function

What will you do as an Accounts Assistant?
- Process high-volume purchase invoices, matching to purchase orders and delivery notes
- Reconcile supplier statements and resolve invoice and payment queries
- Prepare weekly and monthly supplier payment runs
- Monitor outstanding customer balances and assist with debt collection
- Maintain fixed asset registers and assist with depreciation journals
- Assist with stock reconciliations and inventory reporting

What do you need as an Accounts Assistant?
- Previous experience in an Accounts Assistant or Finance Assistant position
- AAT Level 3 qualified or equivalent practical experience
- Good understanding of purchase ledger, sales ledger and bank reconciliations
- Good IT skills, particularly Microsoft Excel
- Strong organisational skills, accuracy and attention to detail

title: Accounts Payable Administrator
description:
Accounts Payable Administrator
Location: Redditch
Salary: 26,000 per annum
Working arrangements: Hybrid working (2 days a week in the office) and flexibility

Flora Partners are recruiting for an Accounts Payable Administrator to join a friendly and supportive finance team based in Redditch.

This is a great opportunity for someone with previous accounts payable or invoice processing experience who is looking to build on their existing skills or simply enjoy a better work-life balance.

The business offers a flexible working environment, with the opportunity to develop and progress for someone who wants to, although progression is certainly not an expectation.

As an Accounts Payable Administrator, you will support the day-to-day running of the purchase ledger function, ensuring invoices are processed accurately and efficiently.

Your responsibilities will include:
- Processing supplier invoices accurately and in a timely manner.
- Matching invoices against purchase orders and resolving discrepancies.
- Handling supplier queries and liaising with internal departments.
- Supporting supplier statement reconciliations.
- Ensuring invoices are correctly coded and authorised.
- Assisting with payment runs and maintaining accurate supplier records.
- Identifying and resolving invoice discrepancies.
- Providing general administrative support to the wider finance team.

Ideally, you will:
- Have previous accounts payable, purchase ledger or invoice processing experience.
- Demonstrate excellent attention to detail and accuracy.
- Be organised and able to manage your own workload.
- Have good communication skills and be confident handling queries.
- Be comfortable using finance systems and Microsoft Excel.
- Enjoy working as part of a team whilst also being able to work independently.
- Have a positive, proactive and adaptable approach.

In return, you will:
- Receive a salary of 26,000 per annum.
- Benefit from hybrid working and flexibility.
- Join a friendly and supportive finance team.
- Enjoy a good work-life balance.
- Have the opportunity to develop your skills and progress, should you wish to.

Interested?

Please apply with your CV for further information.

Applicants must have the right to work in the UK.

title: Finance Assistant
description:
About the Business

A great opportunity to join a large, well-established services business based in Worcester as a Finance Assistant, paying £27,000 - £31,000 per annum, with hybrid and flexible working. Reporting to an Assistant Management Accountant, you'll support month end and reporting for the wider finance team. The role suits someone who is AAT qualified, studying, or keen to start.

Main Duties:

As a Finance Assistant, your main duties include:
- Posting journals, recharges and everyday accounting adjustments accurately and within agreed deadlines
- Helping to prepare accruals, prepayments and supporting schedules during month end
- Keeping financial records, working files and backing documents complete and up to date in the finance and reporting systems
- Assisting with balance sheet and control account reconciliations, looking into routine differences and raising anything that needs escalating
- Helping to put together the monthly management accounts packs and other reports
- Pulling together records and evidence for both the internal and external auditors
- Following finance policies and controls, and flagging errors, exceptions or possible control issues
- Getting involved in process improvements and team projects that make finance more efficient
- Building your knowledge of accounting principles, controls, reporting and the finance systems
- Supporting wider projects across the business when needed

Location / Office / Culture

The role is hybrid, based in Worcester, with three days a week in the office and very flexible working. You'll be part of a larger finance team, working closely with the management accountants and learning the month-end process from start to finish.

What We Are Looking For

The ideal candidate will have:
- Previous experience in a finance role is essential
- Experience processing and checking financial information accurately
- Experience using an ERP or finance system
- GCSE English and Maths at grade 4/C or above (or equivalent)
- AAT qualified, currently studying, or keen to start
- Comfortable working to deadlines and prioritising your own workload
- Able to look into problems and work out what has gone wrong
- Strong attention to detail, good communication skills and basic Microsoft 365

Why Join the business
- Hybrid working, three days in the office
- Very flexible working
- Study support
- Broad exposure to month end, reconciliations and audit
- A solid grounding for a future management accounting career
- Large, well-established business

About Us

title: Payroll Administrator
description:
Payroll Administrator

An initial 6 month role with possibility of going permanent

Up to 27k + increments upon completing training

5 days on site for 3 months

Location: Worcestershire

Hours: Full-Time, 37.5 Hours per Week (Monday to Friday)

Salary: Competitive, dependent on experience

We are recruiting on behalf of our client for a Payroll Administrator to join their Finance team. This is an excellent opportunity for a detail-oriented and organised professional looking to develop their career within payroll, supporting both UK and international payroll operations.

Working closely with an experienced payroll team, you will help ensure payrolls are processed accurately, compliantly and on time, while providing a high standard of service to internal stakeholders, contractors and external providers.

The Role

The successful candidate will support the delivery of an effective payroll service across multiple payrolls and jurisdictions.

Key responsibilities include:
- Assisting with the accurate and timely processing of payrolls.
- Working alongside senior payroll colleagues to ensure payroll deadlines are met.
- Liaising with employees, contractors and external providers to resolve payroll-related queries.
- Supporting the administration of international payrolls through third-party payroll providers.
- Assisting with compliance requirements and payroll documentation for overseas jurisdictions.
- Ensuring timesheets, invoices and expense information are received and processed on schedule.
- Maintaining payroll records and systems with a high degree of accuracy.
- Monitoring payroll processes and identifying opportunities for improvement.
- Supporting business managers by communicating payroll issues and contractor-related concerns.
- Keeping informed of relevant legislative changes affecting payroll, tax and employment practices.
- Providing excellent customer service to both internal and external stakeholders.

About You

We are seeking a highly organised individual with strong administrative skills, excellent attention to detail and a proactive approach to problem-solving.

Essential Skills & Experience
- Strong verbal and written communication skills.
- Excellent organisational skills with the ability to prioritise workloads effectively.
- Strong customer service focus.
- Ability to investigate and resolve problems logically.
- High levels of accuracy and attention to detail.
- Good working knowledge of Microsoft Office, including Word, Excel and Outlook.
- Self-motivated with the ability to work independently and as part of a team.

Desirable Experience
- A minimum of 12 months' payroll experience or experience in a similar finance or administration role.
- Exposure to payroll systems and payroll processing.
- Experience working with international payrolls would be advantageous.

Qualifications

GCSEs (or equivalent) including English Language and Mathematics at Grade C/4 or above.

Additional Advantage

Spanish language skills would be highly advantageous, particularly when supporting international payroll activities and communicating with overseas stakeholders.

Why Apply?

This is an excellent opportunity to join a growing and collaborative organisation where you will gain exposure to both UK and international payroll operations. The role offers variety, responsibility and the chance to develop specialist payroll knowledge while working alongside experienced professionals.

If you are an organised administrator with payroll experience and a passion for accuracy and customer service, we'd love to hear from you. Apply today for a confidential discussion.

title: Payroll Administrator
description:
Payroll Administrator
Redditch £30,000 Full Time, Permanent

Are you highly organised, confident working with Excel, and experienced in managing administrative queries and timesheet data?

An established employer is seeking a Payroll Administrator to support the smooth running of the payroll process. Reporting to the Payroll Manager, you'll play a key role in maintaining accurate records, processing timesheet information, resolving payroll-related queries, and ensuring data is accurate and up to date.

This role would suit someone who enjoys working with spreadsheets and data, has excellent attention to detail, and thrives in a fast-paced environment where accuracy and organisation are essential.

The Role
As Payroll Administrator, you'll provide vital support to the Payroll function, ensuring payroll information is collected, checked, and processed accurately. You will be responsible for managing employee queries, maintaining records, and producing accurate data for payroll processing.

Key Responsibilities
- Managing payroll and administrative queries from employees and managers in a professional and timely manner
- Collecting, reviewing, and validating timesheets, overtime submissions, absence records, and payroll amendments
- Maintaining and updating payroll data using Excel and SAGE
- Investigating and resolving discrepancies, ensuring data accuracy at all times
- Producing reports, spreadsheets, and payroll information to support payroll processing
- Processing new starter, leaver, and employee change documentation
- Maintaining accurate employee records and electronic filing systems
- Liaising with managers across multiple sites to obtain outstanding information and timesheet submissions
- Preparing letters, forms, and supporting documentation as required
- Handling sensitive and confidential information with professionalism and discretion
- Providing general administrative support to the Payroll and wider People function

About You
To be successful in this role, you will have:
- Strong Excel skills, including experience working with spreadsheets, data validation, and reconciliations
- Previous experience in payroll administration, timesheet processing, workforce administration, or data administration
- Experience managing a high volume of queries via email and telephone
- Excellent attention to detail and a methodical approach to administration
- Confidence working with numerical data and identifying discrepancies
- Strong organisational skills with the ability to prioritise multiple tasks and deadlines
- Good communication skills and the ability to build relationships across the business
- A professional and confidential approach when handling sensitive information
- A positive, proactive, and team-oriented attitude

Desirable Experience
- Experience working with large datasets and maintaining accurate records
- Knowledge of payroll processes and employee administration
- Experience within a multi-site business environment

What's on Offer?
- Competitive salary dependent on experience
- Company pension scheme
- Employee benefits programme
- Ongoing training and development opportunities
- Flexible working pattern
- Casual dress
- Free onsite parking

Apply Today
If you're a highly organised and people-focused administrator looking for a varied role within a growing organisation, we'd love to hear from you.
